# Averitt expands logistics network with Jackson, Mississippi, facility

 August 27, 2026 

Less-than-truckload carrier Averitt said Thursday it has opened a 100,000-square-foot distribution and fulfillment facility in Jackson, Mississippi. The announcement follows other recent investments the carrier has made to its network.

The new warehouse is near central Mississippi’s major freight lanes of I-20 and I-55. The Mississippi Department of Transportation announced Tuesday a $400 million project to improve the roadways and bridges along these corridors. The plan also calls for rail upgrades.

Most national LTL carriers have nearby service centers and Averitt operates a 57-door LTL terminal next to the new facility. 

Cookeville, Tennessee-based Averitt’s latest addition will serve rail connections and provide service to ports in New Orleans and Mobile, Alabama. Customers will be able to flex the amount of space needed for seasonal and overflow inventory projects without committing to long-term contracts.

# Rohlig SUUS opens new logistics hub in Szczecin to boost regional connectivity 

 

> Rohlig SUUS opens new logistics hub in Szczecin to boost regional connectivity 

Rohlig SUUS Logistics has opened a new logistics center in Szczecin, strengthening its operations in Poland and improving links with Scandinavia and Western Europe.

The new facility combines warehouse and cross-dock terminal functions. It replaces two previous locations, allowing the company to improve efficiency and streamline operations.

The site covers around 15,500 square metres. It includes 12,000 square metres of warehouse space and nearly 3,000 square metres of cross-dock area. The facility offers around 13,000 pallet positions and features 22 loading docks and a 40-metre external ramp.

The hub is located in the Kostrzyn-Słubice Special Economic Zone, close to key transport routes S3 and A6. This position supports efficient distribution across Poland, Scandinavia and Western Europe, as well as connections to nearby seaports. Operations are set to begin in the second half of May.

# Seino Transportation completes new terminal in Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, with an attached 4 m2 company-owned warehouse. 

August 20, 2026 / Logistics facilities

Seino Transportation announced on August 20th that it has completed construction of its "Ichikawa Branch New Terminal" in Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture.

Facility appearance

The facility was constructed on the former site of the Ichikawa branch in Hon-Gyotoku, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. With the addition of a five-story warehouse and terminal, the facility now serves not only as a branch but also as a warehouse.

Due to the rebuilding of the former Ichikawa branch, the branch functions had been temporarily moved to Urayasu. However, with the completion of the new building, the branch functions will be returned to Ichikawa City, and the new Ichikawa branch will begin operations on August 24th.

DP World Hits 500,000 TEUs on GCC Overland Network, Adds Trucks and New Container Depot

DP World Moves 500,000 TEUs Across GCC Overland Network Since March This Year

GCC road network now supports 3,000 truck movements a day as DP World expands inland logistics capacity

TLME News Service

Published on: 

26 Aug 2026, 5:19 am

DP World has moved 500,000 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) across the GCC through its road and rail network since March this year, giving customers more routing options amid disruption to regional shipping routes.

The milestone reflects the growing use of DP World’s inland logistics network as cargo owners and shipping lines seek alternative ways to move goods across the region. 

The network now supports around 3,000 truck movements a day, with DP World recently adding 700 trucks to expand cross-border and domestic freight capacity.

Ahmad Yousef Al-Hassan, CEO & MD, DP World GCC, said: “Moving half a million TEUs overland shows the scale, resilience and flexibility of our network beyond the terminal gates.
